verifications.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:7fd1a89ca090dbdea5ae9f014853684239cbf80e89dc5cce50914155cb9d484a (source fe22d759, 544 files). I recomputed it in the working tree and in a disposable clone at HEAD 68fe3394, which adds only delivery metadata. I tested against disposable PostgreSQL 16 clusters with LANG unset (SQL_ASCII) and with LANG=C.UTF-8 (UTF8). Both runs gave identical results.
(1) My round-9 repro, zz-sec-r9-probe.test.ts S10, rerun unchanged, now PASSES in both runs. POST /api/v1/does-not-exist, POST /does-not-exist, PUT and DELETE on {T}/evidence, each sent text/plain, JSON or application/octet-stream, with and without a session: 404 every time. Round 9 gave 400 validation.content_type for octet-stream.
(2) Code. decideMediaType (media-types.ts:224-240) returns 'unmatched-route' when request.is404 is set, before any media-type check. assertDeclaredMediaType (:246-255) then deletes the Content-Type, and the preParsing hook (:296-309) sets Connection: close. I read fastify 5.6.1 to confirm the 404 path. handleRequest sees no Content-Type and calls contentTypeParser.run('') when a body is present. getParser('') matches no registered parser: only application/json and application/octet-stream are registered, and there is no catch-all. run() then hands is404 requests straight to the not-found handler (lib/contentTypeParser.js:177-181). So restrictParserTo, the round-9 root cause, can no longer be reached for an unmatched route.
(3) Adversarial probe zz-sec-r10-probe.test.ts:
- P4a (inject): 4 unmatched method/URL pairs x 7 Content-Types (HTAB, unterminated quote, */*, a latin1 charset, multipart, urlencoded, none) all gave 404 not_found with Connection: close and no error log.
- P4b (llhttp): Content-Length of 10 GB or 900 MB, Expect: 100-continue, and a chunked body that never ends all gave a prompt 404 (first byte within 3 ms), never 413 or 400, and the server closed the socket.
- P4c (llhttp keep-alive smuggling): I hid a signed-in logout in the body of an unmatched route (Content-Length, no Content-Type, chunked, and duplicate Content-Type), then pipelined a GET. The server sent exactly one response (404), then closed. GET /me still answered 200 afterwards, so the hidden request never ran.
- The rate limiter still precedes the refusal (P3b).
The candidate's own regression tests (media-types.test.ts, 'an unmatched route is 404 not_found whatever its body', 3 tests) pass in both locales.

Verified on the same candidate (sha256:7fd1a89c..., source fe22d759) in both locale runs.
(1) My round-9 repro, zz-sec-r9-probe.test.ts S11. Its assertion expected the HTAB spelling to be REFUSED with a detail naming octet-stream. It now 'fails' because the request is ACCEPTED: 'application/octet-stream\t; x=1' gives 200, stored byte-exact, with the sha256 of the raw bytes, in both framings (r9 S1 rows). This is the finding's second suggested remedy: the essence check and the parser lookup now agree. It is the genuine fix, not a regression, and that S11 assertion is obsolete.
(2) The detail half of the finding (every refusal names the operation's declared set).
- Code: mapError maps FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE to undeclaredMediaTypeProblem(consumesOf(request)) (hooks.ts:68-71). frameworkProblem threads the request through. decideMediaType and restrictParserTo use the same helper.
- P1: 19 spellings x 2 framings on uploadEvidenceContent. Each malformed one (OWS around '=', an empty value, no '=', an unterminated quote, a trailing backslash, a space inside type/subtype, a JSON essence, a list, a comment, NUL) gives 400 validation.content_type 'Send the request body as application/octet-stream.', declared, with nothing stored.
- P1b (llhttp, obs-text): the same detail.
- P4d (llhttp, two identical Content-Type lines; malformed): the same detail, then close.
- P6b: the FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE backstop names octet-stream for an octet route, and falls back to JSON without throwing when the route has no config.
(3) Agreement between the check and the lookup.
- Accepted headers are rewritten to the canonical 'essence[; name=value]' form (media-types.ts:163-165, 252) before handleRequest reads request.headers, which is raw.headers because nothing sets additionalHeaders. Only this code writes request headers (diff-scan.log).
- P6 fuzz: 20,000 random Content-Type strings over a hostile alphabet, against both declared sets. 1,760 were accepted and 38,240 refused, with 0 mismatches against fastify 5.6.1's getParser prefix rule. Every refusal names the route's set.
- P1: quoted ';', an escaped quote, a quoted ' application/json', HTAB on both sides, leading or trailing OWS, empty parameters and X="" are all stored byte-exact.
- P2: UTF-8 JSON in every legitimate spelling is created verbatim.
